newsitem.title: USA: Regulatory bills to pass in '97 - US congressmen.
newsitem.headline: Regulatory bills to pass in '97 - US congressmen.

text.p: Legislation to ease federal regulations on the oil industry and other businesses should pass in Congress next year, several congressmen told the Independent Petroleum Association of America Wednesday.
"We believe we'll have the votes to deal with regulatory reform in the next Congress," Alaska Republican Sen. Ted Stevens said at an IPAA news conference.
Rep. Bill Brewster, an Oklahoma Democrat, said relief from federal regulatons "would keep the stripper wells going" in parts of Oklahoma and Texas.
Rep. Jim Chapman, a Texas Democrat, said regulatory reform advocates were "greedy" this session, trying to get too many changes too quickly.

While he said proposing a comprehensive bill to put more cost-benefit restrictions on regulations "is what we really need to engage the debate," he said advocates might also do well to put regulatory checks in individual pieces of legislation,

Also at the news conference, Texas Republican Sen. Phil Gramm said he will push a bill to eliminate the administration's power to set extra fees on transporting hazardous materials, such as fuels, which he said has become a hidden taxing mechanism.
